description_full: D.R. Horton, Inc. operates as a homebuilding company in East, North, Southeast, South Central, Southwest, and Northwest regions in the United States. It engages in the acquisition and development of land; and construction and sale of residential homes in 128 markets across 38 states under the names of D.R. Horton. The company also constructs and sells single-family detached homes; and attached homes, such as townhomes and duplexes. In addition, it provides mortgage financing and title agency services; and engages in the residential lot development business. Further, the company develops, constructs, owns, leases, and sells multi-family and single-family rental properties; conducts insurance-related operations; and owns water rights and other water-related assets, as well as non-residential real estate, including ranch land and improvements. It primarily serves homebuyers. D.R. Horton, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Arlington, Texas.

financial_summary: D.R. Horton, Inc. is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $38.9B market cap on $33.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -2% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 24% against a 10% cost of capital — a 14-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $3.3B in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.21× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 10.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 11% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
